people.story: Howard Frank Magwire was born on New Year's Day 1919 in Springfield, Vermont, one of twin boys born that morning to Frank A. Magwire and Alice (Bates) Magwire; his twin was Harold Charles. The town's own printed register of births for 1919 lists the two boys one above the other. Howard grew up in a family well known in Springfield: his father ran Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield for thirty seven years. On October 16, 1940, aged 21, he registered for the draft, living at 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield, with his mother Mrs. Alice Bates Magwire as the person who would always know his address, and working at the Fellows Gear Shaper Company on River Street. A Veterans Affairs listing shows Army service from August 15, 1943 to January 7, 1946. By 1967 Howard was living in West Springfield, Massachusetts. On January 7, 1961 he married Gwendolyn Farr in Springfield, Vermont, and their daughter Tracy married Rick Crosby. Gwendolyn died before him. Howard died on September 26, 2014 (the Veterans Affairs listing gives the day) and was laid to rest in Oakland Cemetery in Springfield, beside his parents' lot. [^s01] [^s10] [^s13] [^s61] [^s63]

people.story: Gwendolyn Farr was born in Springfield, Vermont, in 1927, a daughter of Harry James Farr and Mary Abbie (West) Farr; her brother Richard's 2009 obituary names those parents. Family tradition: West cousins remembered summer visits with Aunt Abby and Uncle Harry. That memory is not on the map. On January 7, 1961 she married Howard Frank Magwire in Springfield, and they made their home in West Springfield, Massachusetts. Their daughter is Tracy Jo Crosby. Gwen loved quilting, knitting and sewing, walks with her husband and coffee with friends, and was remembered for her ever present smile. After many years of congestive heart failure she died at Suffield, Connecticut, on September 6, 2009, after 48 years of marriage. Services were private. [^s36] [^s27] [^s10] Her Vermont birth record, found in November 2026, confirms that she was born on July 1, 1927 at Springfield Hospital, the first child of Harry J. Farr and M. Abbie West. [^s50]

people.story: Frank Albert Magwire was born on February 14, 1889 in Springfield, Vermont, the son of Albert A. Magwire and Alice Jenny (Spaulding) Magwire. He graduated from Springfield High School in 1909 and on July 10, 1912 he married Alice Evadna Bates in Springfield; the marriage appears in the town's printed register for that year. In June 1917 he registered for the draft at Woodsville, New Hampshire, aged 28, as a druggist supporting a wife and one child, and described as short and slender with light gray eyes and brown hair. He trained as a pharmacist and registered in Vermont, and in 1914, while working in Charlestown, New Hampshire, just across the Connecticut River, he was granted a New Hampshire license by reciprocity. For thirty seven years Frank owned and ran Magwire's Pharmacy in Springfield, retiring in 1954. In 1940 he kept three state licensed pinball machines in the store, and when the village demanded its own large license fee he paid under protest and sued; in January 1941 the Vermont Supreme Court reversed the dismissal of his suit and sent it back for trial. He belonged to St. John's Lodge No. 41 F&AM and Independent Order of Odd Fellows Lodge No. 42 for more than fifty years, was a 32nd Degree Mason and a member of Mt. Sinai Shrine in Montpelier. Frank and Alice raised three sons: Raymond (born 1913) and the twins Harold and Howard (born January 1, 1919). Frank died at Springfield Hospital on October 8, 1967 and was buried in Oakland Cemetery. [^s02] [^s13] [^s18] [^s43] [^s53] In October 1940 all three of his sons named him or his wife as the person who would always know their address, at 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield. [^s60] [^s61] [^s62]

people.story: Alice Evadna Bates was born on September 7, 1889 in Williamstown, Massachusetts. She married Frank Albert Magwire in Springfield, Vermont, on July 10, 1912, and spent the rest of her life in Springfield, where she raised sons Raymond, Harold and Howard. She died on March 29, 1972 and is buried with Frank in Oakland Cemetery. Her own parents have not yet been identified; her Williamstown birth record has been requested. [^s02] [^s14] [^s13] Her son Howard's 1940 draft card names Mrs. Alice Bates Magwire, mother, at 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield. [^s61]

people.story: Albert A. Magwire was born on October 10, 1845 in Brooklyn, New York. His 1887 marriage card names his parents as George and Mary (Prentis), and his 1929 death card gives his mother's maiden name as Mary Prentiss and his father as unknown, so George is probable and Mary is firm. On November 8, 1887, a musician aged 40 on his second marriage, he married Alice J. Spaulding; the card was recorded at Springfield, Vermont, which settles an earlier note that said Cavendish. They made their home in Springfield, where their children Ethel, Frank Albert, Edna, Charles E. and Harrold were born. Albert was in the music trade: in 1904 he ran the Springfield Music Rooms as an Edison phonograph dealer, gave twice weekly outdoor evening phonograph concerts that August, and on October 25, 1904 gave a ticketed phonograph concert in Ludlow Town Hall with two young pianists. Albert died in Springfield on February 21, 1929, aged 83 years, 4 months and 11 days, a music teacher, and is buried in Oakland Cemetery. [^s15] [^s16] [^s18] [^s13] [^s44] [^s58] [^s59]

people.story: Alice Jenny Spaulding was born on August 17, 1866 in Cavendish, Vermont, the fourth daughter of Charles Elliot and Amantha (Putnam) Spaulding. Two separate family histories, the Spalding Memorial of 1872 and the Dickey Genealogy of 1898, list her birth date. She married Albert A. Magwire in Cavendish in November 1887 and raised her family in Springfield. She died on November 13, 1951 in West Lebanon, New Hampshire, and was buried with Albert in Oakland Cemetery, Springfield. [^s06] [^s07] [^s16]

people.story: Charles Elliot Spaulding was born on July 24, 1833 and married Amantha Putnam in Springfield, Vermont, on March 25, 1856. He farmed in Cavendish, where the couple raised Addie Cora, Ida Jenny (who died young), Anna Emma, Alice Jenny, Frank Charles, Lilla May and Gertie Inez. The Spalding Memorial of 1872 traces him eight generations back to Edward Spalding, the immigrant ancestor of the American Spaldings; that pedigree is still a lead. Charles died on March 26, 1890 and is buried in Cavendish Village Cemetery. [^s06] [^s07] [^s17]

people.story: Amantha Putnam was born on September 9, 1837, a daughter of Timothy Putnam and Betsey Hall according to the Dickey Genealogy. She married Charles Elliot Spaulding in Springfield, Vermont, in 1856 and lived in Cavendish for most of her life. She outlived her husband by thirty six years, dying in Proctorsville on May 30, 1926, and rests beside him in Cavendish Village Cemetery. Timothy Putnam and Betsey Hall are named only in that compiled genealogy, so they are not drawn on the tree. [^s07] [^s06] [^s17]

people.story: Raymond Bates Magwire, the eldest son of Frank and Alice Magwire, was born in Springfield, Vermont, on March 18, 1913. In 1936 he was a junior at Springfield College in Massachusetts. On October 16, 1940, aged 27, he registered for the draft from 1 Capitol Hill, Fair Haven, Vermont, as a student at Springfield College, naming his father Frank Albert Magwire, of 13 Whitcomb Street, Springfield, as the person who would always know his address. He served as a private first class in the U.S. Army in the Second World War. He made a career in physical education, and by 1952 he was Vermont's state director of health and physical education in the State Department of Education at Montpelier, where he was still living in 1967. He died on April 26, 1997, in Rutland according to Find a Grave, and is buried in Hillside Cemetery, which a Veterans gravesite record lists as at Fair Haven and which is physically in Castleton. His Social Security claims index entry names his parents as Frank A. Magwire and Alice Bates. [^s12] [^s13] [^s45] [^s46] [^s62] [^s64] [^s65]

people.story: Harold Charles Magwire was born on January 1, 1919 in Springfield, Vermont, the twin brother of Howard. On October 16, 1940, aged 21, he registered for the draft in Springfield, naming his father Frank Albert Magwire, of 13 Whitcomb Street, as the person who would always know his address, and working at the Fellows Gear Shaper Company on River Street. He served in the U.S. Navy and married Nellie Magwire. Her details are not published. He died in Ormond Beach, Florida, on October 16, 2002. He is buried in the Vermont Veterans Memorial Cemetery at Randolph Center. [^s01] [^s11] [^s60]

people.story: Harry James Farr was born in Denver, Colorado, on April 3, 1888, the son of George Oscar Farr (born in Westfield, Massachusetts) and Alice Beard (born in Andover, Vermont), according to his 1926 marriage card and his 1966 death certificate. He served a year as a corporal in the Vermont National Guard and was discharged in July 1913. On December 4, 1912 he married Laura Mary Seward in Springfield, Vermont; that marriage ended in divorce. By June 1917 he was a letter carrier for the U.S. Post Office in Bridgeport, Connecticut, living at 276 Gregory Street. He was back in Springfield by 1926, and on August 11, 1926, at Chester, Vermont, he married Mary Abbie West of Chester Depot. Their daughter Gwendolyn was born in 1927, Richard in 1930, and Alma later. In 1942 he lived at 6 Bridge Street, Springfield, and worked for the U.S. Post Office Department on Main Street, Springfield; in 1950 he was 62 and living in Springfield. The card that follows his 1942 card in the Vermont set, probably the back of it, describes a man 5 feet 7 inches tall and 142 pounds, with blue eyes and brown hair. He died at DeGoesbriand Memorial Hospital, Burlington, Vermont, on May 22, 1966, aged 78, retired and residing at 6 Bridge Street, Springfield, and his death certificate names his wife as Mary Abbie. Family tradition: the family remembered summer days at a West farm in Wells, Maine. That place is only a lead, so it is not on the map. people.story: Mary Abbie West, called Abby in the family, was born in Peru, Vermont, in 1901 or 1902, the daughter of William Wallace West and Alice Dina Waite (born in Dorset, Vermont), according to her 1926 marriage card. She was living at Chester Depot, and is probably the Abbie West paid for teaching in the Chester schools that year, when on August 11, 1926 she married Harry James Farr at Chester; it was her first marriage and his second. She was the mother of Gwendolyn (born July 1, 1927), Richard (born July 1, 1930) and Alma; both children's birth cards give her place of birth as Peru, Vermont. In 1942 Harry named her as the person who would always know his address, and in 1950 she worked as a clerk at the post office in Springfield. Her husband's 1966 death certificate names her as his wife. Family tradition: West relatives remembered a farm in Wells, Maine. That place is not on the map. [^s27] [^s05] [^s36] [^s41] [^s40] [^s49] [^s50] [^s55] [^s57]

people.story: Roy E. Crosby was born on February 25, 1925 and raised in Chicopee, Massachusetts, one of at least nine children of Ernest and Eva (Pierce) Crosby. In the Second World War he served in the U.S. Navy aboard the escort carrier Marcus Island and fought in the Battle of Leyte Gulf in October 1944. He married Dorothy Richardson, and in 1950 they moved to West Springfield, where they raised Robert, Debra, Rick and Lynn. Roy worked as a pressman for the Springfield Newspapers, where he also played AA ball, and finished his career as an HVAC technician at Western New England College. A lifelong Yankees fan, he built a summer home on Otis Reservoir with his family. He died at home on May 2, 2014 after 65 years of marriage and was buried with military honors at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. [^s20] [^s21] [^s23] [^s24]

people.story: Dorothy R. Richardson was born on October 24, 1928 to Robert and Anne (Ernst) Richardson and raised in Chicopee, Massachusetts. She married Roy E. Crosby and moved with him to West Springfield in 1950, where she was a proud homemaker. Like Roy she was a lifelong Yankees fan, and she spent her summers at the family's home on Otis Reservoir. Her brother Robert Richardson and sister Barbara Vogel died before her. Dorothy died in February 2022 and was interred with Roy at the Massachusetts Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Agawam. people.story: Ernest Allan Crosby was born at Norwood, Yarmouth County, Nova Scotia, probably on June 1, 1884 (his 1918 draft card; his 1942 card writes the date as 1/6/1884), the son of James W. and Asenath (Porter) Crosby. Like many young people from Yarmouth County he moved to Massachusetts, and on July 6, 1906, aged 22, he married Eva E. Pierce of Brazil Lake at Wakefield. Their first child, Ruby Evelyn, was born in Wakefield that November. On September 12, 1918 he registered for the draft at Chicopee, living on Luther Street, with Eva Etta Crosby as his nearest relative. The family settled in Chicopee, where they raised at least nine children: Esther, Ruby, Winston, Ivoline, Thelma, Gordon, Muriel, Roy and Bernard. In 1942, aged 57, he lived at 35 Haven Avenue, Chicopee, worked for the A. G. Spalding Company, and named Mrs. Eva Crosby as the person who would always know his address. Eva died in 1944. In the 1950 census Ernest, then 65 and widowed, was still in Chicopee with his daughter Thelma, and with his daughter Muriel and her husband Douglas Rhodes. He died in 1958 and is buried beside Eva in Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield. [^s28] [^s04] [^s22] [^s23] [^s54] [^s56]

She is buried in Hillcrest Park Cemetery, Springfield, Massachusetts. [^s28] [^s22] [^s23] Her husband's 1918 draft card names his nearest relative as Eva Etta Crosby, which gives her middle name. people.story: William Wallace West is named as the father of Mary Abbie West on her 1926 marriage card, which gives his birthplace as a Vermont town whose spelling is hard to read. Nothing else is known yet. [^s49]

people.summary: Alice Dina Waite, born in Dorset, Vermont, was the mother of Mary Abbie (West) Farr.
people.story: Alice Dina Waite, born in Dorset, Vermont, is named as the mother of Mary Abbie West on her 1926 marriage card. Nothing else is known yet. [^s49]

people.summary: George Magwire was the father of Albert A. Magwire.
people.story: George Magwire is named as the father of Albert A. Magwire on Albert's 1887 marriage card, and in a Find a Grave note. Albert's 1929 death card says the father was unknown, so this link is probable. Nothing else is known yet. [^s59] [^s16]

nameVariants.name: Mary Prentis
nameVariants.note: The spelling on the 1887 marriage card.

people.summary: Mary Prentiss was the mother of Albert A. Magwire.
people.story: Mary Prentiss is named as the mother of Albert A. Magwire on two Vermont records: his 1887 marriage card, which writes Mary (Prentis), and his 1929 death card, which gives her maiden name as Mary Prentiss. Nothing else is known yet. [^s59] [^s58]
